    "some": 3.0, "many": 2.7, "any": 2.2, "all": 2.0, "most": 2.0, "one": 1.9,
    "which": 1.7, "each": 1.6, "rest": 1.3, "two": 1.3, "more": 1.3, "majority": 1.0,
    "%": 0.7, "percent": 0.6, "bulk": 0.6, "portion": 0.4, "part": 0.3, "parts": 0.3,
    "end": 0.3, "out": 0.3, "member": 0.3, "members": 0.3, "because": 0.5,
}
OTHER_QUANT = {"three", "four", "both", "none", "several", "few", "either", "lot", "bit",
               "piece", "variety", "type", "range", "example", "examples", "snippet",
               "plenty", "thousands", "half", "much", "number", "kind", "sort", "couple"}
# the 'of' itself: positive after quantity words, negative after counting / collection words
OF_QUANTITY = {"example": 1.5, "examples": 1.5, "snippet": 1.1, "some": 1.2, "bit": 0.8,
               "all": 0.5, "lot": 0.45, "majority": 0.5, "plenty": 0.4, "variety": 0.4,
               "thousands": 0.35, "many": 0.3, "type": 0.3, "range": 0.3, "piece": 0.3,
               "any": 0.3}
OF_COUNT = {"one": -0.7, "those": -0.7, "sequence": -1.0, "array": -0.7, "copy": -0.7,
            "collection": -0.6, "product": -0.45, "list": -0.35, "series": -0.3,
            "end": -0.3, "each": -0.2, "two": -0.2, "three": -0.2}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    cur = s[-1].strip()
    prev = s[-2].strip().lower() if len(s) > 1 else ""
    head = s[-3].strip().lower() if len(s) > 2 else ""
    if cur == "of":
        return None, OF_QUANTITY.get(prev, OF_COUNT.get(prev, 0.0))
    if cur == "the" and prev == "of":
        if head in PARTITIVE:
            return None, PARTITIVE[head]
        if head in OTHER_QUANT:
            return None, 0.8
        return None, 0.1
    if cur == "the" and prev == "all":
        return None, 2.0
    if cur == "the" and prev in ("among", "'s"):
        return None, 1.0
    if cur == "the" and prev in ("to", "on", "and", "as", "or"):
        return None, -0.12
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down_proj, component 4516: a /k/ + /v/ or /w/ sound split across tokens.

The unit goes strongly negative on the token that carries the v- or w-sound of a
k-sound cluster whose k-sound ends the previous token:
  'к|в' (квартира, квадрат), 'k|val' (kvalitet), 'Mosk|va', 'K|wa' (KwaZulu),
  'RK|W' (RKW), 'г|в' (гвоздя, лингвистика).
It also goes negative on katakana ク (ku) followed by a vowel kana in loanwords:
ク|エ (quest), ク|イ (queen).

A k that closes an English syllable ('ck', 'ok', 'lk', 'nk': 'Slack|ware',
'Brook|wood', 'Milk|weed') is left out, since there the w starts a new word.
Everywhere else the prediction is 0. The values are the average activation seen in
training text for each case.
"""

READS = ()

K_SOUND = "kкqг"             # letters that make a /k/ (or /g/) sound: Latin, Cyrillic
V_SOUND = "vwв"              # letters that make a /v/ or /w/ sound
CLOSES_SYLLABLE = "clno"     # letters before a final k in 'ck', 'lk', 'nk', 'ok'
KATAKANA_KU = "ク"
KATAKANA_VOWELS = "アイエウォワ"
KV_VALUE = -5.0              # mean activation on k + v/w boundaries
KANA_VALUE = -4.0            # mean activation on ク + vowel kana


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        return None, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[t - 1].lower()
    now = prefix.token_strings[t].lower()
    if not before or not now:
        return None, 0.0
    last, first = before[-1], now[0]
    k_is_open = len(before) < 2 or before[-2] not in CLOSES_SYLLABLE
    if last in K_SOUND and first in V_SOUND and k_is_open:
        return None, KV_VALUE
    if last == KATAKANA_KU and first in KATAKANA_VOWELS:
        return None, KANA_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4518, a mostly-silent component that dips negative on two things.

1. A capitalised "The" that opens a name in the middle of a sentence: a publication, band,
   organisation or title, as in "...journalist at The Observer", "published by The Pragmatic
   Bookshelf", "...a stop at The Landing". Its strength depends on the word before it:
   after a preposition or conjunction ("at", "by", "of", "in", "and", ...) it dips to about
   -4.3; after a comma to about -2.7; after an opening quote or bracket to about -1.3; after
   any other word to about -0.9. A "The" that starts a sentence or line gets 0.
2. A C# using-directive: "using" at the start of a line after a statement (";"), e.g. the
   "using" in "using System;<newline>using System.Linq;", dips to about -10, and the
   "System" right after it to about -4.

Everything else predicts 0. Predictions are in the component's own units (activation).
The rule covers most of the component's variance on the sampled training text; the
individual values are group averages, not fitted to the eval rows.
"""

READS = ()

PREPOSITIONS = {"at", "with", "for", "by", "to", "and", "from", "on", "in", "as", "like", "of", "before"}
OPENERS = {'"', "“", "(", "'"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    before = prev.strip()
    if word == "using":
        return None, -10.0 if ";" in prev else 0.0
    if word == "System" and before == "using":
        return None, -4.0
    if word == "The":
        if before in PREPOSITIONS:
            return None, -4.3
        if before == ",":
            return None, -2.7
        if before in OPENERS:
            return None, -1.3
        if before.isalpha():
            return None, -0.9
    return None, 0.0

"""Blood detector (a negative response on the word "blood").

The component goes strongly negative on the token that completes the word "blood" in
English ("blood", " Blood", "bloody", "bled"), and on the same word in other languages:
German "Blut" (split as "Bl"+"ut"), Spanish/Portuguese "sangre"/"sangue", French "sang"
(only when it means blood), Russian "кровь", Vietnamese "máu", and the Chinese "血".
It is near zero everywhere else, including on the "bl" fragments and other "bl..." words.

The program tracks the letters of the word that ends at the current token (within its
document, so the word is spelled out across sub-word tokens) and, when that word is one of
these, predicts the typical activation for it. Matching is exact on the whole word, so
"bloodshot" does not count as "blood" once "shot" has arrived.
"""

READS = ()

# Word (lowercase letters) -> typical activation on the token that completes it.
BLOOD_WORDS = {
    "blood": -7.2, "bloods": -7.2, "bloody": -7.2, "bled": -7.2, "blooded": -9.0,
    "lifeblood": -6.0, "bleed": -5.0, "bleeds": -5.0, "bleeding": -4.0,
    "blut": -15.0, "sangre": -10.0, "sangue": -9.0, "sang": -2.0,
    "кровь": -3.3, "máu": -5.0, "血液": -6.0,
}
CHARACTERS = {"血": -10.0}  # the single Chinese/Japanese character for blood


def current_word(prefix):
    """The letters of the word ending at the current token, in its document."""
    word = ""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    for text, d in zip(reversed(prefix.token_strings), reversed(prefix.document_ids)):
        if d != doc:
            break
        run = ""
        for ch in reversed(text):
            if not ch.isalpha():
                break
            run = ch + run
        word = run + word
        if len(run) < len(text):  # a non-letter inside this token ends the word
            break
    return word.lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in CHARACTERS:
        return None, CHARACTERS[token]
    return None, BLOOD_WORDS.get(current_word(prefix), 0.0)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4520, a "topology" word detector.

Plain-language summary: this component is almost always silent. It turns strongly
negative while the model is spelling a word from topology, the mathematics of shape
and continuity. Its main trigger is the piece that completes "topolog..." after a
"top"/"Top" start: the "ological" / "ologically" / "ology" / "ologies" pieces in
"top|ological", "List<Top|ology>". A whole-token "Topology" or " topology" also
triggers it at the same strength. Other "topo..." completions (topos, polytop|oid,
topoisomerase, "topo") are negative, about half as strongly. The Chinese word 拓扑
(topology: 扑 after 拓) is strongly negative, and "homeomorphic" is moderately negative.

The one positive pattern is the digit "1" right after "top" (as in "top 1", "top-1",
"top 10" rankings). The first token of each row, which has no context, gets a small
constant offset.

Everything else predicts 0. Reading the text so far:
  word  - the letters of the current word, lowercased; a space or underscore before a
          piece starts a new word, and punctuation or a digit ends it;
  last  - the last whole word, skipping spaces and hyphens, to see "top" before "1";
  prev  - the previous piece, to see 拓 before 扑.
"""

READS = ()

TOPOLOGY_VALUE = -8.0     # word now spells "topolog..."
TOPO_VALUE = -4.0         # word now spells "topo..." but not "topolog..."
HOMEOMORPH_VALUE = -5.0   # "homeomorph..." (homeomorphic)
TOP_ONE_VALUE = 2.5       # digit "1" right after the word "top"
ROW_START_VALUE = 0.15    # first token of a row, which has no context


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word, doc, last, prev = carry if carry else ("", None, "", "")
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        word, last, prev = "", "", ""

    stem = piece.strip(" _-")
    spaced = piece[:1] in (" ", "_")
    before = "" if spaced else word          # a space starts a new word
    after = before + stem.lower() if stem.isalpha() else ""

    value = 0.0
    if len(prefix.token_ids) == 1:
        value = ROW_START_VALUE
    elif piece == "扑" and prev == "拓":
        value = TOPOLOGY_VALUE
    elif piece == "1" and last.endswith("top"):
        value = TOP_ONE_VALUE
    elif "topolog" in after and "topolog" not in before:
        value = TOPOLOGY_VALUE
    elif "topo" in after and "topo" not in before:
        value = TOPO_VALUE
    elif "homeomorph" in after and "homeomorph" not in before:
        value = HOMEOMORPH_VALUE

    word = after
    if stem.isalpha():
        last = word
    elif piece.strip() not in ("", "-", "_"):
        last = ""
    return (word, prefix.document_ids[-1], last, piece), value

"""A pulse at call-like opening parentheses, not at ordinary words.

Attached parentheses after long, compound or object-member names are negative.
Single variables, numbers and control keywords tend positive instead. Quoted
arguments and empty calls weaken the pulse; whitespace usually suppresses it.
The rules below use only surface syntax, with a small one-token continuation.
They do not identify individual APIs or reproduce all their different strengths.
"""
import re

READS = ()
CONTROL = set('''if elif while for foreach switch catch with assert sizeof typeof
    synchronized lock using except lambda'''.split())
MATH = set('''sin cos tan cot sec csc arcsin arccos arctan sinh cosh tanh log ln
    exp max min gcd lcm lim det'''.split())

# Parenthesis forms: offset, strength, member penalty, keyword boost,
# single-variable boost, number boost.
FORMS = {
    'bare':   (.22, 1.15, -1.61, .25, .36, .52),
    'word':   (.29, 1.00, -1.32, 1.04, .64, .62),
    'quote':  (.06, .65, -.48, .03, .21, -.30),
    'symbol': (.19, .85, -.84, .38, .21, -.02),
    'empty':  (-.08, .08, -.03, 0, .02, -.17),
}


def pulse(tokens):
    token = tokens[-1]
    if '(' not in token:
        return 0.0
    head, tail = token.split('(', 1)
    past = ''.join(tokens[:-1])
    if head and not head.strip('>'):
        return -1.60                 # Generic argument list ending in >(
    if head and not head.strip('_'):
        past += head
        head = ''
    if head and not head.isspace():
        return -.04
    markdown = past.endswith('`')
    past = past.rstrip('` ')
    match = re.search(r'[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z_0-9$]*$', past)
    name = match[0] if match else ''
    left = past[:-len(name)] if name else past
    member = left.endswith(('.', '->', '::'))
    camel = bool(re.search('[a-z][A-Z]', name))
    snake = '_' in name
    line = past.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    code = member or camel or snake or bool(re.search(
        r'=|;|\bnew |\bpublic |\bvoid |\bdef |\bconst ', line))
    if head:                         # Whitespace-separated parentheses
        if name == 'return':
            return .66
        if name in ('for', 'foreach'):
            return .36
        if name == 'catch':
            return .08
        return -.04 + ((.07 - .072 * min(20, len(name))) if code else 0)

    if tail.startswith(')'):
        form = 'empty'
    elif tail.startswith(('"', "'", '\\"', "\\'")):
        form = 'quote'
    elif not tail or tail == '\\' or tail[0].isspace() or tail[0] == '`':
        form = 'bare'
    elif tail[0].isalpha() or tail[0] == '_':
        form = 'word'
    else:
        form = 'symbol'
    chars = pieces = 0
    for part in reversed(tokens[:-1]):
        if chars >= len(name):
            break
        chars += len(part)
        pieces += 1
    constructor = bool(re.search(r'\bnew\s*$', left))
    base = (-.07 * bool(name) - .05 * min(24, len(name))
            - .24 * min(5, pieces) - .68 * camel - .29 * snake
            - 1.08 * constructor - .31 * code + .27 * name.isupper())
    offset, gain, member_weight, keyword, variable, number = FORMS[form]
    value = (offset + gain * base + member_weight * member
             + keyword * (name in CONTROL) + variable * (len(name) == 1)
             + number * bool(past and past[-1].isdigit()))
    value += .44 * (name in MATH) - 1.08 * markdown
    value += 1.23 * (tail in ('s', 'es') and len(name) > 3
                    and name.islower() and not code)  # Optional plural suffix
    value += .69 * (name == 'pub')                    # Rust visibility
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, [], 0.0, False)
    _, history, previous, continuing = carry
    token = prefix.token_bytes[-1].decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    history = (history + [token])[-21:]
    current = pulse(history)
    value = current + (.18 * previous if continuing and ')' not in token else 0)
    continuing = '(' in token and ')' not in token
    return (doc, history, current, continuing), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4526 -- a 'be-' word-fragment detector (negative direction).

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on a token that starts a word
with the letters "be" and continues into something unusual or unfinished, such as
"bed" in "/testbed", "bes" / "bek" / "beb" / "besch" inside German or Swedish words,
or a capitalised "Be" or "BE". It stays near zero on "be" inside ordinary words such
as "because", "between", "begin", "beta", "began" and "better", and on most other
text. It also dips a little on the two-dot leader "··".

How the program guesses it, from the token text alone (no context except the one
previous token, used for "test"):
  * "··" or "·"                                  -> -0.9
  * a common whole word (beta, begin, because...) -> 0
  * the bare piece "be"                           -> -1.4 if capitalised,
                                                    -0.8 if attached to a word,
                                                    -0.15 if it is a spaced lowercase " be"
  * "be" + consonant, e.g. bed, bes, beb, bek, best, beck, beth
      - "bed" right after "test" (testbed)          -> -3.0
      - other "bed"                                 -> -1.3
      - a spaced token " bes", " best"              -> -1.3
      - an attached token "bes", "best"             -> -2.5
  * anything else                                   -> 0

Why: the activation is mostly the token's own spelling (a lookup over tokens explains
about half the variance on held-out text, this rule about a third). The rule keeps
the strong, frequent cases and leaves out what a table would add: the many
rarer fragments, and the within-token variation that depends on wider context.
"""
READS = ()

# letters that, after "be", mark an unfinished fragment rather than a common word
CONSONANTS = set("bcdhkstwz")
# complete English words that start with "be" and do not fire
WHOLE_WORDS = {
    "beta", "began", "begin", "begun", "because", "between", "besides", "better",
    "before", "below", "beyond", "bench", "been", "being", "beat", "bell", "berry",
    "bend", "beige", "belly", "beverage",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s = tok.strip().lower()
    spaced = tok[:1].isspace()
    capital = tok.strip()[:1].isupper()
    if s in ("··", "·"):
        return carry, -0.9
    if not s.startswith("be") or s in WHOLE_WORDS:
        return carry, 0.0
    if len(s) == 2:
        if capital:
            return carry, -1.4
        return carry, (-0.15 if spaced else -0.8)
    if len(s) <= 5 and s[2] in CONSONANTS:
        if s == "bed":
            if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower().endswith("test"):
                return carry, -3.0
            return carry, -1.3
        return carry, (-1.3 if spaced else -2.5)
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 4527: a document-start and code-string detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
  1. First token of a document (or of a packed row): the component is driven by the
     token itself. Comment/header starts ('#', '##') push it strongly negative, as do
     code and prose openers such as 'import', 'package', 'The'; a leading space pushes
     it mildly positive.
  2. Inside a document it is mostly quiet, with three weak-to-strong responses:
       - the terminator word EOF of a shell heredoc (`<< 'EOF'`) fires strongly;
       - an opening quote or quote-paren such as ("  ('  (\\"  in a print/log/echo call
         fires moderately;
       - indentation (a run of spaces or tabs) fires weakly, more so at the start of a
         block after '{', ':' or ';'.
Everything else predicts 0.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Activation at the first token of a document, by token.
FIRST_TOKEN = {"#": -1.3, "##": -1.3, "import": -0.9, "package": -0.6, "The": -0.35,
               " ": 0.35, " of": 0.3}
FIRST_OTHER = -0.2  # other first tokens

PRINTING = re.compile(r"print|log|echo|<<|cout|println|printf", re.I)
BLOCK_END = re.compile(r"[{:;]\s*\n?[ \t]*$")
RECENT = 40  # characters of recent text kept in the carry


def _is_indent(tok):
    return len(tok) >= 2 and tok.strip() == "" and "\n" not in tok


def _is_quote_opener(tok):
    return len(tok) <= 4 and (any(c in tok for c in "\"'`") or tok == "(f")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or doc != carry[1]:
        recent = ""
        value = FIRST_TOKEN.get(tok, FIRST_OTHER)
    else:
        recent = carry[0]
        value = 0.0
        if tok == "EOF" and "<<" in recent:
            value = 2.0
        elif _is_quote_opener(tok):
            value = 0.35 if PRINTING.search(recent) else 0.0
        elif _is_indent(tok):
            value = 0.1 if BLOCK_END.search(recent) else 0.04
    recent = (recent + tok)[-RECENT:]
    return (recent, doc), float(value)

"""A coarse fantasy/videogame vocabulary detector.

It groups words by familiar meanings, using WordNet for inflections and kinds
and CEDICT glosses for Chinese. Decaying fantasy/game cues modulate later
word weights. Names are case-sensitive; split English words are joined
so 'elf' in 'self' is not mistaken for a fantasy creature. Colon-ended labels
have a small separate response. Weights are fitted by semantic group, not
by token identity; their overall gain is calibrated on training interventions.
This deliberately leaves idiosyncratic token responses out.
"""
import regex as re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
import cedict

FIELDS = (
    'superhero mutant cyborg vampire werewolf zombie demon dragon goblin elf '
    'orc troll fairy wizard sorcerer witch ghost phantom genie monster creature',
    'alien extraterrestrial robot android sentient',
    'magic magical enchant summon teleport immortal resurrection reincarnation '
    'supernatural superhuman paranormal necromancer',
    'gameplay videogame rpg mmorpg pokemon minecraft roblox bukkit '
    'warcraft dota genshin fortnite yugioh nintendo xbox playstation',
    'marvel avenger batman superman spiderman hulk thor buffy naruto '
    'goku vegeta transformers dalek tardis torchwood potter',
    'game gaming gamer player npc character avatar roleplay hero heroine '
    'villain protagonist antagonist',
    'quest dungeon raid melee ranged loot inventory exp xp mana guild '
    'stamina stats respawn spawn',
    'boss arena combat battle fight attack weapon armor duel sword',
    'power ability skill spell curse transform',
    'level health damage speed effect attribute strength',
    'world universe realm dimension galaxy kingdom empire',
    'comic cartoon anime manga animation animated crossover fanfic fantasy '
    'fiction fictional sci-fi',
    'episode series saga season',
    'chapter scene novel story cast',
    'appearance outfit personality costume form shape body',
    'map item client packet entity mod plugin server chunk sprite',
    'real normal usual ordinary strange weird imaginary reality',
)
SETS = tuple(frozenset(f.split()) for f in FIELDS)
N = len(SETS)
AMBIGUOUS = set('character level power world cast real normal usual ordinary '
                'health damage client packet entity server item map series story '
                'spell curse spirit form body strength season shape speed'.split())

@lru_cache(maxsize=150000)
def classify(word, translate=False):
    word = word.lower()
    if translate:
        glosses = cedict.glosses(word)
        if not glosses and len(word) > 1:
            # Tokenization sometimes attaches a grammatical particle to a noun.
            if any('particle' in g for g in cedict.glosses(word[0])):
                glosses = cedict.glosses(word[1:])
        gloss = ' '.join(glosses).lower()
        words = set(re.findall(r'[a-z]+', gloss)) - AMBIGUOUS
        if 'character (in' in gloss or 'role (in' in gloss:
            words.add('character')
    else:
        words = set(wordnet.base_forms(word)) | {word}
    out = [float(bool(words & s)) for s in SETS]
    if not translate and word.isalpha():
        if wordnet.is_a(word,'mythical_being'):
            out[0] = 1.0
        if wordnet.is_a(word,'fictional_character'):
            out[4] = 1.0
        if wordnet.is_a(word,'weapon'):
            out[7] = 1.0
    return tuple(out)

@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def token_features(text):
    text = re.sub(r'([a-z])([A-Z])', r'\1 \2', text)
    out = [0.0] * N
    words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+|\p{Script=Han}+', text)
    for word in words:
        for i,x in enumerate(classify(word,not word.isascii())):
            # Proper names, unlike ordinary 'marvel' or 'transformers'.
            if i == 4 and word.isascii() and not word[0].isupper():
                continue
            out[i] = max(out[i], x)
        # A name split across tokens can already be recognizable from its stem.
        if len(word) >= 4 and word[0].isupper():
            if any(name.startswith(word.lower()) for name in SETS[4]):
                out[4] = 1.0
    return tuple(out)


def features(carry, prefix):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', 0.0, 0.0)
    _, previous, topic, code_topic = carry
    current_text = text
    # An English suffix such as "elf" in "self" is not a fantasy noun.
    continuing_word = (previous and text and text[0].isascii()
                       and text[0].isalpha() and previous[-1].isascii()
                       and previous[-1].isalpha() and not text[0].isupper())

recognizes double middle-dot punctuation.

    set("""the and is are was were to of for with that this it as on be
        have has from not by but an you your we they he she his their
        which will would can""".split()),
    set("""el la los las de del una un y que por para con se es en no
        como su al lo ha""".split()),
    set("""o a os as de do da dos das um uma e que por para com em no na
        não ao se é são""".split()),
    set("""di che il la per una un si non sono con della delle dei del nel
        nella al alla lo da le gli è""".split()),
    set("""le la les de des du un une et est que qui dans pour pas au aux
        il elle avec ne ce sur en à""".split()),

    sich és az hogy egy mint meg vagy bir bu için ile olan olarak
    çok daha gibi değil sen biz""".split())
FUNCTION_WORDS += (OTHER_WORDS - set().union(*FUNCTION_WORDS),)

SHORT_IBERIAN = set("ser ter haber poder caer ir ficar".split())

estar tener hacer fazer essere avere fare dire decir andar venir andare
venire aller ver voir vedere être avoir faire querer deber saber vouloir
pouvoir devoir savoir llevar mantener obtener seguir poner perder mover
""".split())

    r"(.*(?:ar|er|ir|or|ur))(se|si|me|mi|te|ti|lo|la|li|le|ne|nos|os|mos|em|m|s)$"
)

@lru_cache(maxsize=16000)
def plausible_infinitive(word, language):
    if word in {"per", "par", "pour", "sur"}:
        return False
    if language in {"es", "pt"}:
        if not word.endswith(("ar", "er", "ir")) or word.endswith("uer"):
            return False
    form = word
    if language == "it" and word.endswith("r"):

            return False
        form = word + ("re" if word.endswith(("dur", "por")) else "e")

        # These other-language cues receive a stronger veto.
        votes[-1] += 2 * (token in FUNCTION_WORDS[-1])

    language = LANGUAGES[index]

    romance = 1 <= index <= 4 and votes[index] >= 2
    romance = romance and votes[index] > non_romance + 0.5

    joined = (previous if continuing else "") + text

            elif word in SHORT_IBERIAN:
                value = -4.3 if language in {"es", "pt"} else -1.0
            elif language == "it" and word == "fare":
                value = -4.4

"""A coarse predictor of prose punctuation and linking-word responses.

Group tokens by grammatical role and punctuation type. Increase the estimates
in text with spaced blank paragraphs, archaic words, or semicolons together
with frequent "the"/"of". Add bonuses for four short grammatical patterns.
Also distinguish abbreviation periods, period-dashes, and the third digit
of a number beginning with 1 (a pattern often found in years).
Individual words and genre remain approximate.
"""
READS = ()

RELATIVES = set('which who whom whose qui que'.split())
CONJUNCTIONS = set('and or but et'.split())
MODALS = set('can could may might must shall should will would'.split())
COPULAS = set('am is are was were be been being have has had'.split())
PREPOSITIONS = set('of to in on at by for with from upon into over under '
                   'through out about between as'.split())
DEMONSTRATIVES = set('this that these those'.split())
POSSESSIVES = set('my your his her its our their'.split())
PRONOUNS = set('I you he she it we they me him us them'.split())
ARTICLES = set('a an the all any some each every no'.split())
DEGREE = set('very much less more most rather quite nearly almost '
             'certainly probably really'.split())
ARCHAIC = set('thou thee thy thine hath doth unto whilst amongst '
              'thereof wherein therein upon'.split())
ABBREVIATIONS = set('Mr Mrs Ms Dr Prof Rev St Jr Sr etc pp p vol al v'.split())

LEVELS = {
    'spaced_paragraph': (-0.104, -0.104),
    'third_digit': (0.206, 0.818),
    'digit': (0.0, 0.03),
    'period_dash': (0.815, 0.758),
    'abbreviation_period': (0.15, 0.746),
    'sentence_newline': (0.017, 0.079),
    'newline': (-0.004, -0.003),
    'semicolon': (0.06, 1.086),
    'comma': (0.035, 0.561),
    'sentence_end': (0.021, 0.588),
    'space': (-0.003, 0.139),
    'other': (0.0, 0.028),
    'capitalized_word': (-0.001, 0.017),
    'content_word': (0.006, 0.163),
    'relative': (0.17, 0.689),
    'conjunction': (-0.012, 0.162),
    'modal': (0.045, 0.32),
    'auxiliary': (0.019, 0.276),
    'preposition': (0.006, 0.315),
    'demonstrative': (0.026, 0.376),
    'possessive': (0.006, 0.164),
    'pronoun': (0.008, 0.167),
    'article': (0.008, 0.23),
    'degree': (0.078, 0.672),
}
BONUSES = {
    'clause_conjunction': (0.08, 1.185),
    'relative_article': (0.469, 0.338),
    'prepositional_pronoun': (0.064, 0.329),
    'pronoun_auxiliary': (0.033, 0.42),
}


def token_kind(s, previous, digits):
    word = s.strip()
    if s == ' \n\n':
        return 'spaced_paragraph'
    if s.isdecimal():
        if len(digits) == 2 and digits[0] == '1':
            return 'third_digit'
        return 'digit'
    if s.startswith('.-'):
        return 'period_dash'
    if s == '.' and (previous.strip() in ABBREVIATIONS or
                     (len(previous.strip()) == 1 and previous.strip().isalpha())):
        return 'abbreviation_period'
    if s and not any(c.isalnum() for c in s):
        if '\n' in s:
            return 'sentence_newline' if '.' in s else 'newline'
        if ';' in s:
            return 'semicolon'
        if ',' in s:
            return 'comma'
        if '.' in s or '?' in s or '!' in s:
            return 'sentence_end'
        if s.isspace():
            return 'space'
    if not (s.startswith(' ') and word.isascii() and word.isalpha()):
        return 'other'
    for name, words in WORD_CLASSES:
        if word in words:
            return name
    return 'capitalized_word' if word[0].isupper() else 'content_word'


WORD_CLASSES = (
    ('relative', RELATIVES), ('conjunction', CONJUNCTIONS),
    ('modal', MODALS), ('auxiliary', COPULAS), ('preposition', PREPOSITIONS),
    ('demonstrative', DEMONSTRATIVES), ('possessive', POSSESSIVES),
    ('pronoun', PRONOUNS), ('article', ARTICLES), ('degree', DEGREE),
)


def observe(carry, s, document):
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        carry = (document, '', '', 0, 0, 0, 0, False)
    _, previous, digits, n, articles, semicolons, archaic, spaced = carry
    n += 1
    articles += s in (' the', ' of')
    semicolons += s == ';'
    archaic += s.strip().lower() in ARCHAIC
    spaced |= s == ' \n\n'
    article_density = max(0.0, min(1.0, (articles / n - .025) / .05))
    formal = min(1.0, semicolons) * article_density
    style = min(1.0, spaced + .7 * formal + .2 * archaic)
    kind = token_kind(s, previous, digits)
    word, before = s.strip(), previous.strip()
    bonuses = []
    if kind == 'conjunction' and before in (',', ';'):
        bonuses.append('clause_conjunction')
    if word == 'the' and before in RELATIVES:
        bonuses.append('relative_article')
    if kind in ('demonstrative', 'possessive') and before in PREPOSITIONS:
        bonuses.append('prepositional_pronoun')
    if kind == 'auxiliary' and before in PRONOUNS:
        bonuses.append('pronoun_auxiliary')
    digits = (digits + s)[-8:] if s.isdecimal() else ''
    state = (document, s, digits, n, articles, semicolons, archaic, spaced)
    return state, kind, style, bonuses


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    carry, kind, style, bonuses = observe(
        carry, prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.document_ids[-1])
    base, extra = LEVELS.get(kind, (0.0, 0.0))
    value = base + style * extra
    for name in bonuses:
        base, extra = BONUSES.get(name, (0.0, 0.0))
        value += base + style * extra
    return carry, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4538, read as a plain-language rule.

This component is one hidden unit of layer 1's MLP (its input direction is almost
exactly that unit), so its activation is that unit's value, scaled. The unit is a
gate times a value:

- GATE (register of the recent text). It rises with old or literary English
  (function words like "which", "whose", "of", "his", "by", "upon", "thou"; a few
  more such as "he", "was", "at" were also associated with it in the data) and falls
  with code, markup, symbol-heavy text and modern instructional filler ("use", "can",
  "if", "would"). It rises slowly as the document goes on. It is a running average over
  the document so far.
- VALUE (the current token). Punctuation (, ; . ) is strongest, ordinary English words
  next, then digits and code-like tokens, and anything else weakest.
- The first token of each document has its own strong response (about 0.39 on average).

Prediction = 0.42 * silu(gate) * value_of_token - 0.006, except at a document's first
token, which gets 0.39. The largest real activations (2 to 5) come from clause-joining
punctuation and "and"/"which" in long formal prose, which this rule captures only partly.
"""

import math
import re

READS = ()

FORMAL_WORDS = {
    "which", "whose", "whom", "of", "his", "by", "or", "may", "than", "its", "thereof",
    "upon", "whilst", "hath", "doth", "thou", "thy", "ye", "hence", "therefore",
    "whereby", "wherein", "thereby", "shall", "must", "such", "certain", "whole",
    "former", "latter", "said", "he", "was", "at", "no",
}
CODE_WORDS = {
    "use", "can", "if", "new", "would", "about", "so", "is", "each", "will", "not",
    "there", "This", "also",
}
# How strongly each kind of token drives the unit (its up-projection).
VALUE = {"punct": 0.756, "lower": 0.259, "code": 0.133, "other": 0.052}
DOC_START = 0.39
ALPHA = 0.02  # how fast the running averages forget older tokens


def _kind(raw):
    st = raw.strip()
    if st == "":
        return "other"
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]+", st):
        return "lower" if st.islower() else "other"
    if re.fullmatch(r"[.,;:!?'\"]+", st):
        return "punct"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d+", st) or re.search(r"[_/{}()\[\]=<>&|*#$\\@;]", st):
        return "code"
    return "other"


def _looks_code(raw):
    st = raw.strip()
    return bool(re.search(r"[{}\[\]()<>/\\=_:;*#$@|&]|\s{2,}|\t", raw)) or st in CODE_WORDS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc or carry is None:
        formal, code, seen = 0.0, 0.0, 0
    else:
        formal, code, seen = carry

    if new_doc:
        value = DOC_START
    else:
        gate = 8.9 * formal - 1.47 * code + 0.06 * math.log1p(seen) + 0.106
        value = 0.42 * gate / (1 + math.exp(-gate)) * VALUE[_kind(raw)] - 0.006

    # update the running register with this token (it counts for later positions)
    formal = (1 - ALPHA) * formal + ALPHA * (raw.strip() in FORMAL_WORDS)
    code = (1 - ALPHA) * code + ALPHA * _looks_code(raw)
    return (formal, code, seen + 1), float(value)

What it does: this component fires on the vowel-glide sound "oy" (as in "toy", "boy",
"Roy", "joy", and "oj" spellings) when it is spelled inside a short token, and on a
y/j-type glide written directly after an o-letter at a token boundary, as in the
French "Royaume" split as "ro" + "ya". Russian "оя" (as in "стоя", "про|яв")
and an exact "ой" token also fire, more weakly. Everything else is about 0.

The predicted activation is a rule, not a learned table. The rules are:
  1. The token, lowercased and stripped, is a short oy/oj word: an optional
     single leading consonant, then "oy" or "oj", optionally followed by "s"
     (toy, Boy, roy, oj, toys). Activation about 6 when the token has no
     leading space, about 3 when it does (" boy" is weaker than "boy").
  2. The token contains "оя" (Cyrillic o + ya): about 5.
  3. The token starts with a glide letter (y, j, я, ю, й, ї) and the previous
     token ends in an o-letter (o, ó, ō, ø or Cyrillic о), with no space
     before the glide: about 4. Examples: "ro|ya", "Y", "ja", "яв".
  4. The token is exactly "ой": about 1.5.

The rules are hand-written from the component's activations on 4096 training
rows. Whole-token identity explains more, but it would need a table of token
ids with no concept behind it, so the rules stay as the explanation.

Measured on 1024 eval rows: variance explained 0.38, r 0.62. The rules
explain only the big spikes; the many tiny activations (|a| < 0.3) are left
at 0. Known misses: contexts that change the size of an "oy" spike, and a
few non-glide tokens such as "ystick" after "Jo".

READS = ()

OY_WORD = re.compile(r"^[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz]?o[yj]s?$")

O_LETTER = set("oOоОóÓōøØ")

    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().lower()

    elif raw[:1] in GLIDE and prev[-1:] in O_LETTER:
        value = 4.0

    return carry, value

    "class def function const let var public private protected static "
    "void int float double bool string".split()

    value += 0.022 * (bool(w) and not w.strip("$"))

    value -= 0.009 * (word in {

    value -= 0.036 * (word in {"maybe", "perhaps", "possibly", "probably"})

        prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]

What it does: almost everywhere this component is near zero noise (std about 0.05) with no
compact pattern in the tokens, so the program predicts 0 there. Its one large, clean response
is to a document made only of the middle-dot filler token "··" (two U+00B7 characters). At
the first "··" of such a document, and at every later "··" while nothing but "··" has come
before it in that document, its activation is about 1.085. Once any other token appears,
the response drops back to 0.

attention see only that token, which produces this fixed, large value. It is a rare
degenerate case, not a general feature of the model.

Reset it at each row start and each document change.

SPIKE = 1.085  # the activation on a filler-only document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]

    all_filler = all_filler and prefix.token_strings[-1] == FILLER

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4542: a weak "file extension" detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Negative on a file extension written as one token, such as `.json`, `.yml`,
  `.txt`, `.sh`, `.mod`, `.rs`, `.md`, `.go` or `.py`. Data, config and build-file
  extensions (json, yaml, cfg, txt, sh, jar, mod, ...) are the most negative;
  source-code and document extensions (rs, go, py, js, md, ...) are less so.
  The push is stronger when the file name sits in a path: a `/` or `\\` appears
  in the few tokens before it.
- Positive on the name of a programming language used as a word or path piece,
  such as `/python`, `-go`, `Java`, `typescript`, `Php` (not after a dot).
- Positive on "that" right after a preposition ("in that", "of that", "for that").
- Strongly positive on the horizontal-bar symbol `⎯`.
- Zero on every other token.

Why: the activation is mostly small and spread over thousands of token types.
Its large values come from the token types named here, so this program captures
the few concepts that carry the most variance and predicts zero elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

# Data, config and build-file extensions: most negative.
DATA_EXTENSIONS = set(
    "json yml yaml xml csv cfg conf ini toml mod jar so sh txt spec properties "
    "lib o out dat tom cpp".split()
)
# Source-code and document extensions: less negative.
CODE_EXTENSIONS = set(
    "rs go py c h hpp java rb php js ts tsx jsx css html md pdf log util".split()
)
LANGUAGES = set(
    "python go java php typescript javascript ruby rust cpp golang react node js ts py "
    "c# csharp swift kotlin perl scala haskell lua".split()
)
PREPOSITIONS = set("in of for to but on at with by from".split())
BAR = "⎯"


def _in_path(prefix, window=8):
    """True if a slash or backslash token occurs within the last few tokens of the same document."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    for i in range(len(prefix.token_strings) - 2, max(-1, len(prefix.token_strings) - 2 - window), -1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != doc:
            break
        if "/" in prefix.token_strings[i] or "\\" in prefix.token_strings[i]:
            return True
    return False


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token == BAR:
        return carry, 0.6
    if token.startswith("."):
        ext = token[1:]
        if ext in DATA_EXTENSIONS:
            value = -0.3
        elif ext in CODE_EXTENSIONS:
            value = -0.12
        else:
            return carry, 0.0
        return carry, value * (1.3 if _in_path(prefix) else 0.7)

        if prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1] and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() in PREPOSITIONS:
            return carry, 0.15

        return carry, 0.1
    return carry, 0.0
